The original localhost:4000 paper body was unreachable at reconstruction time, so this is rebuilt from those sources and the built code — not a byte-copy of the lost original. Canonical ledger: the hyperquiz-epic task tree on guerrilla.

The core scaling truth: individual live cursors are O(N^2) bandwidth — every player's pointer must reach every other screen, so cost grows with the square of the crowd. That gives a practical ceiling of a few hundred concurrent pointers before the fan-out saturates.

Below a crossover threshold the Room streams individual cursors (the spectacle). Above it, the Room switches to an O(1) 32x32 heatmap — a fixed 2,048-byte payload regardless of player count. Same swarm-feel on the projector, constant cost.

items.value: Threshold: @heatmap_threshold 300 (room.ex), with a live set_heatmap_threshold/2 setter — runtime-tunable, not a recompile.
Test-pinned on both sides of the crossover (individual below, heatmap above).
Target: ~2,000 players per room on a SINGLE node. Postgres carries content and results; the realtime fan-out is in-memory in the Room GenServer.

blocks.content: Multi-node sharding (hq-p7-shard) is PARKED. Decision B holds that a single node covers the ~2,000/room target; sharding unparks only if a MEASURED load ceiling on guerrilla demands it, not on speculation. Region placement needs nothing new — guerrilla already exists.
